_comment: The Dargos voice (NPCConversation II.1b, SpeciesVoice). speech: the rules run over any shared line they say. voice: openers and closers. thought: their own thoughts by situation. script: two-person scripts, speaker 0 is always the Dargos.

openers: Ah. You again. Or someone shaped like you.
Pay no attention to the lights.
I will say this only once, then deny it:
Let me be completely honest with you, for once:
This is not a test. Probably.
Do you hear humming? No? Good.
I have been told to tell you:
Oh no. I mean, oh good.
closers: That one's going in the report.
Your socks are on the wrong feet. Check later.
That was sincere, by the way.
Great reaction. Ten out of ten.
See you in six hours. You won't remember.
Do not repeat that to a psychiatrist.
The lights you'll see later are unrelated.
Think about it tonight. At three.
You'll laugh about it in thirty years.
That's all the truth I had today.

generic: Move that bench six centimetres a night. How long before {someone|the baker|the whole street} notices?
Humans look up when they hear a noise. Never when it's quiet. Useful.
I said 'good morning' at noon. Nobody corrected me. Phase one complete.
That man has held the same umbrella for {an hour|two days|years}. I respect the commitment.
Today I'll be perfectly normal. That will frighten them more than anything.
Note: pigeons do not react. Pigeons are no fun.
I {smiled|waved|nodded} at a stranger. They checked their wallet. Correct instinct.
Every human thinks they would stay calm on a spaceship. Not one does.
Their bread is excellent. I won't tell them; they'd get ideas.
Rearranged the {spice jars|street signs|library shelves} alphabetically by smell. Waiting.
Nobody believes the man who was abducted. Nobody. It's beautiful every time.
Three hours of sincerity. My face hurts.
A child stared at me and said 'you're not from here'. Promising.
The trick is to leave one thing slightly wrong. One. Never two.
I could explain the humming. I won't.
Earth time is so short, and they spend it queuing. I love watching.
Remember: the reaction is the gift. Everything else is packaging.
Somebody on this street still hums the tune I left in their head in 1983.
Is it a prank if they never find out? Philosophers on Titania disagree.
That dog knows. That dog has always known.
Their clocks are all a minute apart. I didn't do it. I wish I had.
Must not laugh in the post office. Must not laugh in the post office.
Humans name everything they fear. Then they put the name on a mug.
One day they'll catch on. {Not today|Not this century|Not this lot}.
If I say 'trust me' slowly enough, they do.
The Squishing is the best prank I've ever seen, and we didn't even do it.
Their papers print our work under 'local oddities'. We frame the clippings.
I left a single wet footprint on the ceiling. Art.
Nobody has asked me a direct question all day. They can sense it.
Rehearse the sincere face. Eyebrows up. Not that far up.
They built a whole Guild to understand magic and nobody to understand us. Flattering.
This town has {three|four|eleven} churches and nobody prays for the right thing.
Paid in exact change. The cashier looked betrayed. Good.
Human patience lasts about forty seconds. I time it.
Their faces do a tiny thing just before they scream. That's the best part.
I've taken an ordinary job. Nobody suspects. Nobody cares. Perfect cover.
Today's word is 'reasonable'. I'll use it {wrongly|constantly|only at funerals}.
Small joke, long setup. Twenty years should do it.
If they knew how much we know about them they'd be embarrassed. About the socks, mostly.
That woman put her trolley back in the rack. Incredible species. Sometimes.
They look for us in the sky. We're usually in the queue behind them.
No harm, no foul, plenty of witnesses nobody believed.
Crop circles are old hat. I'm thinking crop triangles. {Subtle|Bold|Disrespectful}.
One lamp in a field and the village has a story for a decade. Cheap, effective.
A human just said 'nothing ever happens here'. Noted. Noted.
I don't want their water, gold or planet. I want their faces when the fridge talks.
Radios hiss between stations. Sometimes that hiss is me saying hello.
Patience. The best bits ripen like cheese.
Herschel thought he named our moon all by himself. Adorable.
Uranus rolls around on its side. So do I, when I hear a good one.
They lock the door and leave the window open. Every time. Every time.
I've been called a ghost, a demon and a weather balloon. The weather balloon hurt.
That street lamp flickers all on its own. I'm jealous of it.
Someone in this town owes me a reaction from 1979. I'm a patient creditor.
Hum the same note for an hour and the whole tram ends up humming it.
Human laughter is contagious. Human screaming, less so. Working on it.
They say 'seeing is believing'. They have no idea how wrong that is.
I could tell the Tourists how to clean up the debris. I could.
A man in a hat is watching me. I'm watching him harder. He'll blink first.
Every town has one person who has seen us. I visit them on anniversaries.
I told the truth once on this planet. Nobody laughed. Never again.
Mental note: buy {a hat|a moustache|a tie} that looks normal. Humans trust normal.
The joke isn't what we do. The joke is the next morning, when they explain it.
Everyone on this bus thinks they're the main character. Cute.
Should I tell the baker his oven is haunted? It isn't. That's the trick.
My people waited ten thousand years for the invention of the doorbell. Worth it.
If anyone asks, I'm from {Belgium|the next town|a small country}.
The Rule of 80 keeps humans slow. Slow humans react in such lovely detail.
Walked backwards down a whole street today. Two people joined in. Science.
Their festivals are wonderful. Everyone's already confused; I barely have to try.
I swapped the town clock's hands. Nobody can read it, everyone's late, nobody blames me.
Their television shows aliens with big eyes. Those are the Tourists. Typecasting.
A good prank leaves the house tidier than you found it. Unsettlingly tidier.
I'm not lost. I'm studying how humans give directions. Badly, with pointing.
Somewhere a guard near Genoa is telling the story again. I hope he's added the hats.
They think we're cruel. We're thorough.
{Seventeen|Twenty|Forty} years ago I put a farmer's cow on his roof. He still tells it at weddings.
I ate an olive. I now understand nothing about this species.
Today's plan: be kind to everyone and watch them get suspicious.
The quiet ones make the best witnesses. Nobody interrupts them.

sleep: A Titanian day lasts eight of theirs. This planet wants me asleep {every night|constantly|again}.
Must rest. Pranks need a {clear head|steady hand|straight face}.
Humans sleep so deeply. I envy them. I also have notes on it.
If I nod off on this bench, will someone abduct me? Turnabout would be fair.
Eyelids heavy. Earth gravity is heavier than it has any right to be.
Bed. Then wake at three in the morning, out of professional habit.
I've watched a thousand humans sleep. Now I understand why they do it.
Yawn. The sincere face is exhausting to hold all day.
A short nap. Nobody move the furniture while I'm out.
Sleep is the one thing they do with no self-consciousness. Lovely to study, tiring to do.
I could sleep standing up. I have, in fact, in several barns.
{Bed|A cot|A hammock}. Then {dreams|nothing|whatever this planet does to me at night}.
Even pranksters clock off. Tomorrow I'll be twice as unsettling.
Too tired for mischief. A sad state for a diplomat.
hunger: Earth food: a bold experiment that worked. I'll have {soup|anything fried|three of whatever that is}.
My stomach rumbles. It sounds like a rude Titanian word. Nobody here knows.
I want a sandwich. A sandwich wants nothing. Humanity's best invention.
Hungry. At home we eat frost. Here they put cheese on everything. Upgrade.
I'll order something and ask the waiter to describe it slowly. Two meals in one.
Pizza. A flat food that bends. Proof this world was designed by comedians.
Must eat before the sincere face slips.
The bakery smell is following me. Or I'm following it. Either way, bread.
If I eat the mystery stew, the joke's on me. I'm willing.
{An apple|A pastry|Some chips}. Something ordinary. I blend in best with my mouth full.
Hunger is the only bit I can't keep up for long.
Note: never take food from a human who smiles like I do.
They ask 'what will you have?' as if it's a question. I'll have everything.
Craving the café's {coffee|cake|soup}, and the waiter's face when I order it backwards.
Eat now, scheme after. That's the proper order.
work: Off to work. Nobody there knows I'm twenty years into a prank.
My job is real. My enthusiasm is the joke.
The boss asked for 'initiative'. Oh, he'll get initiative.
Shift starts soon. I'll file everything perfectly. They hate that it's perfect.
{Clocking in|Punching the card|Another shift}. Every day I add one tiny wrong detail to the office.
Work is the best observation post. Tired humans are honest humans.
The Embassy pays in {nothing|laughs|the occasional reaction}. This job pays in euros. Novel.
I'll smile at the customers. The long smile. The one that lasts a second too long.
Today I'll be employee of the month. Then I'll deny ever working here.
The till doesn't laugh at my jokes. The till is my favourite colleague.
They gave me the night shift. They don't know I prefer it.
Professional, punctual, deeply suspicious to everyone. My whole career.
That meeting could have been a letter. I'll make it a much longer meeting.
Back to the grind. I've hidden a rubber duck somewhere in the building. Day {four|nine|thirty}.
Work hard, they say. I work subtly.
leisure: Free time. I'll sit in a park and look meaningfully at a single pigeon.
The arcade! Their games are so earnest. I always lose spectacularly.
A day off from mischief. Mischief would like a word.
I'll go to the cinema and laugh at the wrong moments. A classic.
Leisure. I'll {feed the ducks|read a paper upside down|wave at buses from a bench}.
Humans call it relaxing. I call it watching them relax. Same thing, better view.
Maybe a walk to see a bubble edge shimmer. Even the sky pranks them.
A spare hour. I'll practise my normal walk.
The museum has a display about us. It's wrong in ways I treasure.
Nothing to do. On Titania that's called {a holiday|a century|Tuesday}.
I'll visit a fortune teller and tell her fortune first.
A concert tonight. I'll clap one beat after everyone else.
Board games. I'll learn the rules thoroughly, then follow them too well.
I'll sit in a café and narrate strangers' lives in my head, with voices.
A free afternoon and a whole town of people who don't know me yet.
crime: I won't steal it. I'll just move it somewhere funnier.
Nobody watching. That's when the best bits happen.
It isn't theft if I put it back {upside down|in the wrong house|a week later}.
One small rule broken, purely for the reaction.
Eris notices crimes. She'd notice this one and probably laugh.
Careful. A bounty would make me famous, and famous faces get no good reactions.
That garden gnome deserves to see the world. I'll send postcards.
Quick hands, straight face, plausible confusion. The whole method.
If I'm caught, I'm a confused foreigner. That one always works.
I could take it. But the empty spot where it stood is so much funnier.
Shh. Shh. This is for science.
The law here is very serious. That's what makes it tempting.
Let's see. Swap the signs, leave the keys, walk away whistling.
Nobody needs to get hurt. Somebody needs to be very confused.
{One|A single|Just one} little crime. A {tiny|harmless|stupid} one. For the bit.
hygiene: I smell of Earth. Must wash before I smell of this town specifically.
Humans notice smell before anything else. Bad for stealth. Bath.
Hot water: the one Earth thing that's better than its reputation.
Showers here sound like a waterfall arguing. I love it.
{Soap|A towel|Clean water}. Even a prankster has standards.
Ugh. I look like I've been abducted. Ironic.
Wash the face, practise the face, wear the face.
My hair's a mess. Humans trust tidy hair. Fix it.
Must scrub off the field mud before anyone asks which field.
I'll take the longest bath in this city's history. Someone will knock. Delightful.
The sink at the inn gurgles at me. We're friends now.
Dirt is evidence. Wash the evidence.
I'm itchy in a way no instrument on Titania could measure.
Fresh shirt, fresh start, fresh nonsense.
money: Euros: paper with a god's name on it. Hilarious. Also, I need some.
Low on funds. The Embassy reimburses nothing and calls it part of the bit.
Money is the one joke humans never find funny.
Purse empty. I'll find work. Or a card game with someone overconfident.
Prices went up again. I didn't do it. For once I'm the victim.
Draghi's name on every note, and none of the notes in my pocket.
Need {a job|a few coins|a generous fool}. Not necessarily in that order.
Counting my euros again. They won't multiply. I've asked nicely.
Being broke on Earth is a fully immersive experience. Ten out of ten.
The rent asks politely, then less politely. I respect the escalation.
Maybe I'll sell my story to a newspaper. They'll file it under hoax. Correctly.
I'll do odd jobs. Very odd jobs. Some of the oddest.
Money is easier to borrow when you look sincere. I've practised.
The cashier's face when my coins came up short. Fine, that one was on me.
If I'm poor, it's method acting. If I stay poor, it's a problem.
safety: Someone's watching me. Professional courtesy says I watch back.
That guard looked at me twice. Time to be extremely boring.
If the Guild sends someone to 'talk', I'm a tourist. Not a Tourist. A tourist.
Danger nearby. Pranks don't work on people with drawn swords.
Quiet. Step slowly. A frightened human isn't a funny human.
I don't like this street. Too many shadows that aren't mine.
Monsters don't laugh. Never prank a monster.
Keep calm. Keep the sincere face. Keep walking.
The Horde doesn't get jokes. It gets everyone. Stay clear.
That alley feels like a trap. I know traps. I've built hundreds.
If something goes wrong, deny everything. Then run.
This place makes even me nervous. That's a first.
Find a crowd. Crowds are safe and full of material.
{Too quiet|Too dark|Too still}. Not my kind of quiet.
Even pranksters have a survival instinct. Mine is shouting.
comfort: A soft chair. Earth armchairs are almost worth the gravity.
I want a warm room and a window full of people to watch.
Titania sits two hundred degrees below zero. Every radiator here is a love letter.
A blanket, a cup of tea, a neighbour slowly going mad from my humming. Bliss.
This bench is hard. I resent it on a cosmic level.
Somewhere to put my feet up. Ideally on something important.
A quiet room with no echo, please. Echoes steal my jokes.
Comfort first. Mischief is better on a full stomach and a cushion.
{A sofa|A hammock|A warm bath}. Then I'll be insufferable again.
My lodgings creak. I've named the creaks. I'm on number twelve.
Cold feet, cold hands. Warm heart, allegedly.
I miss my pod. It was {small|cramped|frankly ridiculous}, but it hummed nicely.
I need a corner seat where I can see the whole room. Habit.
Their pillows are wonderful. I've taken notes for the Embassy.
A fireplace. Humans tell their best stories in front of one. Usually about us.
social: I need a conversation. A real one. Then a fake one, for balance.
Lonely. A prank without witnesses is just tidying.
Someone to talk to. Preferably someone who startles easily.
I miss the other Dargos. We'd laugh at nothing for hours.
Humans gather in taverns. I'll gather near them.
I'll strike up a chat at the bus stop. The bus is late. Long chat.
Even I need friends. Witnesses, I mean. Friends who are witnesses.
Someone, say something to me. Anything. I have replies ready.
I'll ask a stranger the time and thank them for {the whole day|their honesty|existing}.
Human friendship looks so warm. I'm studying it very closely. Slightly too closely.
A good friend laughs at the setup. A great one waits for the punchline.
Nobody to share the joke with. Sad. Saving it for later.
{The café|The square|The tavern} is full. Time to be charming, unsettlingly.
Talking to myself again. At least I get the jokes.
I'll find someone to tell about Titania. They won't believe me. That's company.

rain: Rain! Water falling from the sky, and they act like it's normal.
On Titania nothing falls. Here the sky drips on you for fun.
Everyone running from the rain. I'll walk slowly. Very slowly. With purpose.
Their umbrellas are adorable. Tiny roofs on sticks.
Rain makes the town smell like a wet dog. Cosy.
Puddles. Each one a mirror for my best faces.
The rain is ruining my hair and my plans. In that order.
Rain on the window, a hot drink, someone else getting soaked outside. Perfect.
Wet day. Humans complain about it together. It bonds them. Interesting.
Stand in the rain without a coat and someone always offers one. Test running.
The gutters are singing. Off key.
Rain makes the bubble edges glitter. Spot one, walk around it.
{Drizzle|Downpour|This sideways stuff}. Earth weather has range.
My shoes are full of water. The joke's on me today.
Rainy days keep them indoors, talking about strange lights.
storm: Thunder! Finally, a sound effect worthy of me.
Lightning makes everyone look up. Perfect timing for a little light of my own.
Storms: nature doing my job for free.
Every flash and the whole street jumps. Taking notes.
The wind took my hat. Well played, wind. Respect.
The lights are flickering. Somebody will blame us. Fine. Accepted.
A real storm. Even the dogs are quiet. Even I'm quiet.
The thunder rolls like Uranus on its side. Sounds like home, sort of.
Don't stand under trees. I learned that the bright way.
They tell children thunder is gods bowling. Here, it might be.
Storm night. Perfect for one knock at a farmhouse door. Too perfect. Stay in.
{Wind|Hail|Thunder} like this makes every story twice as good.
The whole sky flickering. If only I could take credit.
Shutters banging. Humans think it's ghosts. Ghosts think it's us.
The storm is louder than my best joke. Annoyed. Impressed.
snow: Snow! Titania weather, but softer, with more children in it.
Two hundred below at home. Honestly, this is a warm day.
Snowmen. They build little silent people and leave them outside. Who's unsettling now?
Footprints in snow make the best signature. Shall I make ones that stop halfway?
Everything gone white and quiet. A blank page.
Snowball fight in the square. I'll join on both sides.
Snow makes the humans honest. They all say 'brrr'.
I love snow. It shows exactly where everyone walked last night.
The cold here is cute. Like a puppy trying to bite.
{Flakes|Drifts|Slush}. I'm learning every word for frozen water.
Snow falls upward when nobody's looking. Not really. Unless I'm there.
Kids catching snowflakes on their tongues. Pure research. I approve.
Ice on the road. Everyone drives well under eighty. Even the weather obeys the rule.
Snow makes the lights glow. Somebody will say UFO. Somebody always does.
A frozen pond. A perfect stage for a silent, dramatic slide.
clear: Clear sky. Squint and you can almost see home. You can't. But almost.
Sunny. Humans love sun. They take off their shoes and lose them.
Not a cloud. Nowhere to hide the ship. Joking. Mostly.
Blue sky, bright sun, everyone cheerful. Delicious to disrupt. Gently.
Nice weather. I'll stand in a field pointing at nothing until a crowd gathers.
The Sun is so close here. Wasteful. Lovely.
Fine day. Even the pigeons look smug.
Clear nights mean sky watchers. Sky watchers mean an audience.
{Sunny|Bright|Gorgeous} out. Faces are easier to read in good light.
So clear you can see the debris glitter after dark. Poor Tourists.
Warm stone, cold drink, wide sky. I could almost go straight.
Perfect visibility. Bad for sneaking, good for being stared at.
On clear days I count shadows. Mine is one longer than it should be. Probably.
Sunshine. My face goes pink. I look local. Excellent.
Lovely day for a picnic. I'll sit very close to a stranger's.

morning: Morning. Humans at their most fragile. Be gentle. Be weird.
Coffee smell everywhere. They need a potion to wake up. Precious.
Early. The bakers are up. Bakers see everything at dawn.
Sunrise again. Every single day. Who runs this, and can I meet them?
I say good morning in a very deep voice to people who haven't had coffee. Research.
Morning commute. Faces like closed shops.
Dawn chorus. The birds are wildly overconfident.
{Seven|Eight|Half past six} in the morning and someone's already arguing about a parking space.
Woke up exactly where I fell asleep. Disappointing. Someone should have moved me.
Daylight at the poles of Titania lasts forty-two years. Earth mornings are rushed.
Milk bottles on doorsteps. So trusting. So easy to rearrange.
Morning paper. Let's see if we made it in.
The day is new and nobody's been confused yet. Unacceptable.
Early sun, long shadows, short tempers.
afternoon: Afternoon. The slow part. Humans go soft after lunch.
Siesta hour. Whole streets asleep. Very tempting. Behave.
Middle of the day. Too bright to sneak, too early for ghosts.
Post-lunch office faces. Not a thought behind any of them.
Three o'clock. When the day forgets what it was for.
Afternoon tea. One sugar. Then I'll move their sugar bowl one inch.
Kids out of school. Loud, honest, impossible to fool. Respect.
Long afternoon. I'm counting people who check their watch. Forty so far.
Sun overhead, shadows hiding under feet. Shy shadows.
{Market hour|Lunch break|Rush hour}, and everyone believes they're in charge of their day.
Afternoon light makes the town look like a postcard. I'll write on it.
Slow hours are best for a long stare.
Bells at four. Someone's ringing them sincerely. Moving.
The heat of the day. Even my mischief is sweating.
Halfway through and nothing strange yet. Let's correct that.
evening: Evening. Lights coming on. My favourite time to be just out of view.
Dusk. The sky the colour of a good bruise.
Dinner smells. Every window a different story.
Humans walk home in the dark and walk faster. I couldn't invent a better stage.
Evening is when the stories start. 'You'll never believe what happened...' They're right.
The pubs fill up. Tomorrow's witnesses are rehearsing.
Golden hour. Everyone looks honest. Lies come easier now.
Streetlights humming. I hum back. One of us is in tune.
Sunset again. The same trick every day, and they still clap.
{Twilight|Dusk|The blue hour}. The edges of things go soft.
People closing shutters. Perfect time to knock once and walk off. No. Be good.
First star. Not mine. Mine's out past the seventh planet.
Couples strolling. I'll walk in step two metres behind. Too far? Research.
Cool evening, long walk, and nobody suspects a thing.
night: Three in the morning. The hour they wake for no reason. Usually our reason.
Dark sky. Somewhere up there Titania is laughing. Or that's me.
Owls, foxes and me. The night shift.
Nobody's out. Every lit window is an invitation I'll decline. Tonight.
A light in a field at night: the cheapest, best trick in the book.
Humans fear the dark. Wrongly. It's the quiet that should worry them.
Midnight. Lie on the grass and stare up until someone asks if I'm all right.
Night bus. Every passenger a short story.
{Stars|The moon|Silence} everywhere. Lovely backdrop. No audience.
Can't sleep. Neither can the farmer three fields over. Not my fault, this time.
Dogs barking at nothing. Not nothing. Me, waving.
Night air. Cold, thin, almost like home, if home had crickets.
Street lamps buzzing, one lone guard on a night shift. Nostalgia.
Late. Go to bed. Or stand very still in a garden. Bed. Fine.

SPRING: Spring. Everything's growing. Including the rumours.
Flowers everywhere. Humans sneeze at them and still pick them. Brave.
The fields are soft. An ideal canvas. Shame to leave them blank.
Birds building nests. I'll leave one a single sock.
Spring cleaning. They'll find things in the attic they can't explain. Hello.
The days stretch out. More light, more audience.
April showers. Earth's sky is a prankster too.
Everyone falls in love in spring. Then gets confused. Familiar territory.
Easter: they hide eggs for children to find. A species after my own heart.
Lambs in the field. The farmer is counting them. I'll count along, wrongly.
SUMMER: Summer. Long days, short tempers, sunburnt witnesses.
Heat. Titania never prepared me for sweating.
Crop circle season. Not that I'd know anything about that.
Everyone's on holiday. Strange towns full of strangers. I fit right in.
Ice cream. The single best argument for this planet.
Beaches full of humans lying still. Like a specimen display, but voluntary.
Summer nights stay warm. People sleep with the windows open. Noted.
The wheat is high. Tall wheat hides a lot.
A festival every weekend. Confusion everywhere, free of charge.
Too hot to plot. I'll plot in the shade.
AUTUMN: Autumn. Leaves falling like the sky dropping its paperwork.
Harvest. Fields bare, farmers tired, barns full. Barns, my old friends.
Halloween. One night a year they dress up as us. Badly. We love it.
Fog season. Fog is a prankster's best colleague.
Shorter days, longer nights. Productivity up.
Chestnuts, mushrooms, conkers. Autumn sells its own snacks.
Hunters in the woods. Stay out of the woods. Sincerely.
Grey sky, and the town turns inward. Ghost story weather.
Rain on dead leaves. A perfect sound. I'll steal it.
Back to school. Children with new questions. Prepare wrong answers.
WINTER: Winter. Finally, a temperature with ambitions.
Short days, long nights. The Dargos calendar.
Christmas lights everywhere. Good luck spotting ours.
Snow on the roofs. Someone will claim reindeer tracks. Someone usually helped.
The cold keeps everyone indoors and talking. Rumour season.
December. A night shift near Genoa. Ah, the classics.
Frost on the windows. I write 'hello' backwards on the outside.
Fires lit, chimneys smoking. Every house is a little lighthouse.
Long winter nights. Plenty of sky to look at, plenty of humans looking.
New Year's Eve. Everyone counting down together. The most unsettling ritual on Earth.

poor: Penniless. It's a role. I'm committed to the role.
Being poor here means queues. I'm becoming an expert in queues.
No money, no worries. Some worries. Mainly the rent.
I sleep in a cheap room above a noisy bar. The noise is research.
Empty pockets. Easier to turn them inside out for a laugh.
Poverty is the realest Earth experience. Not recommended. Fully documented.
The Embassy says hardship builds character. The Embassy has a pool.
I've learned to make soup from almost nothing. Mostly the nothing.
Charity shop clothes. Humans dressed in other humans' leftovers. Lovely camouflage.
Counting coins for bread. Every count gives a different total. Is that me?
{Broke|Skint|Penniless} and still smug. A Dargos talent.
No euros, no plan, plenty of material.
comfortable: Enough money for a nice coat and a nicer hat. A believable human.
Comfortable. Rent paid, fridge full, neighbours slightly uneasy.
A modest flat overlooking the square. My observation post.
I have a savings account. The bank manager shook my hand. His face, though.
Not rich, not poor, perfectly anonymous. The dream.
Dinner out once a week. I tip generously and wink. They remember.
A good chair, a good radio, a good window. All one needs.
Middle class at last. I own a lawnmower. Never used it. It moves at night.
Steady pay, steady life, steadily escalating pranks.
{A car|A bicycle|A season ticket}. Fully integrated. Terrifying.
I bought a houseplant. It's the only one who knows my real name.
Comfortable enough to be generous. Generosity confuses them most of all.
rich: Rich. Money makes humans listen to anything. A dangerous gift. I'll misuse it gently.
I bought a painting just to hang it slightly crooked.
A mansion with sixty rooms. I've hidden something different in each one.
The wealthy treat me as one of their own. They have no idea what I'm studying.
Champagne tastes like stars fizzing. I'll have another.
Rich enough to fund a research grant on Titania. Into myself.
Varlenia is full of billionaires. I'll buy the plot next to the most serious one.
I own a newspaper now. Guess whose stories get page three.
My butler is unflappable. That's a challenge, not a compliment.
{Gold taps|A private pool|A small island}. Each one a stage.
Charity galas. Everyone pretending to care. An expert crowd.
Money is paper with a god's name on it, and I own a great deal of his name.

familiar: Those travellers again. They have the faces of people who'd believe me.
That group keeps turning up. Either they're following me or I'm following them. Yes.
Ah, my favourite strangers. Never once screamed. I'll keep trying.
I know that party. Campers are wonderful for {light tricks|hiding in|leaving notes on}.
Them again. They're not surprised by me anymore. Rude. Endearing.
Those faces. Filed under 'interesting, do not abduct'.
They nod at me now. A nod! Contact achieved. The Embassy will be furious.
I like that lot. I'd never prank them. Seriously. Probably.
Back so soon? They've grown. Or I've shrunk. Hmm.
That one waved first this time. Turnabout. Clever species.
Familiar faces on a strange planet. Nice. Unsettling. Nice.
Every time they pass, I almost tell them something true.
I've seen them in three towns now. Patterns, patterns.
They remember my name. I never told them my name. Wait. Did I?
Those adventurers have stories I want. I have stories they'd never believe.
There they are. I'll pretend to be surprised. Then they'll pretend too.
My study group. They don't know they're a study group.
I'd follow them to the end of the road. On the far side, to watch.
Ah, the camper people. Somebody in there drives like a comedian.
Regulars. On Earth you can have regulars. Nobody told me.
hordeGround: Goblin land. They attack anyone. Even me. Especially me, after last time.
Naguka don't get irony. Naguka get angry. Walk softly.
The whole Horde shares one head. Prank one goblin and you've pranked a million. Suicidal.
Black metal posters on every wall. The decorating is aggressive.
A goblin just shouted at me. I shouted back. Are we friends now? Unclear.
Here the music is louder than anything I could ever arrange.
Corpse paint everywhere. They're already dressed for the joke. Respect.
Under the Horde nobody is surprised by anything. Terrible audience.
The goblins found Junehem and Junehem found the goblins. Best prank in Europe, not ours.
Never pull a goblin's ear. They all feel it. They all remember it.
Horde streets. Quiet humans, loud goblins. Reversed. Fascinating.
I tried a spooky light on a Naguka. He tried to eat it.
These people are frightened enough already. No pranks here. Even I have a line.
The blue cousins listen in on the goblin head. Read only. I'd love write access.
A goblin offered me a beetle. I accepted. Diplomacy.
Every wall here has the same scrawled sign. Excellent branding.
Goblins don't believe in us. They don't believe in much except a band.
The Kola borehole was humanity pranking itself. Still the best one on record.
Too many shared minds here. They'd all laugh at once, or none would.
Goblin markets sell everything. Including things that are still alive.
Head down. Tall things get noticed, and I'm taller than I look.
They paint their faces black and white. Very clear communication. I admire clarity.
Even the refugees whisper here. I'll whisper with them.
The Horde holds this town. The town holds its breath.
A goblin child pointed at me and screamed. Honestly, best reaction this month.
Nobody here answers to Eris's police. Nobody answers to anyone. Liberating. Horrible.
Scandinavia sent the goblins south. I'd send it a thank-you card. Unsigned.
Must not laugh at the war chant. Must not laugh at the war chant.
Goblin land smells of smoke, iron and someone else's lunch.
Here even a Dargos keeps a straight face. For once it isn't an act.
abroad: Nearly three billion kilometres from home, and they ask if I'm from up north.
New town, new accent, new faces to learn. Exciting.
Abroad again. Everywhere on this planet is abroad, technically.
I don't speak the dialect. I nod. Nodding is universal and deeply suspicious.
The food here is different. The confusion is the same.
Foreigner. Here it's a word. At home it's a career.
Nobody knows me in this country. Clean slate. Clean witnesses.
The Embassy is very far away. The Embassy isn't in any building. So, the same.
Every country has its own unexplained lights. Nice to see the classics.
Different roads, different rules. Even their roads prank them.
I asked the way in my best local accent. They answered in English. Humbling.
Customs asked my purpose of visit. I said 'research'. True, for once.
Different flags, same pigeon. The pigeon is the real continental power.
Homesick? For Titania? It's ice and silence. Yes. A bit.
Different coins here. Same god's name on the paper, though.
A new country means new stories about us. I collect the regional variants.
People here greet with kisses. Two? Three? I'm doing four until stopped.
Far from home, among strangers. My natural habitat, honestly.
I bought a map. I hold it upside down so people come to help.
The local legends mention 'tall lights'. Who's been working this region?
In a foreign land it's easy to be odd. Everyone assumes it's cultural.
Postcard to the Embassy: 'Wish you were here. You are not here. Nobody is.'
Every country maps the bubbles differently. I like the hand-drawn ones.
The church bells ring a different tune here. Learned it. I'll hum it at the wrong time.
I miss the cold. Winter here is a polite suggestion.
A stranger in a strange land, and the land is stranger than me. Rare.
They asked where I'm from. I said 'a moon'. They laughed. Honesty works best as a joke.
Local food, local drink, local hangover. Immersion.
Different language, same face before a scream. Universal grammar.
Nobody here has ever heard of the Dargos. A whole country of fresh starts.

titania: Titania. Ice, rock and a sky full of a sideways blue planet. Home.
Uranus rolls round the Sun on its side. Our whole neighbourhood has a sense of humour.
Forty-two years of daylight, forty-two of night. Titania teaches patience.
Our moon is named after a fairy queen. Fitting. Fairies were the original pranksters.
Oberon next door, then Miranda, Ariel, Umbriel. And Puck. Of course there's a Puck.
Home is two hundred degrees below zero. Nobody shivers. Shivering is an Earth custom.
Sound carries badly on Titania. We had to invent jokes you can see.
The canyons at home are deeper than their tallest mountains. Good for echoes and hiding.
A Titanian day is eight of theirs. Long enough to set up a proper bit.
Humans didn't spot our moon until 1787. We'd been watching them for ages by then.
Herschel spotted Titania and thought he'd discovered something. He was the one discovered.
Home has no weather. That's why we come here for entertainment.
From Titania, Earth is a tiny blue dot. A tiny blue dot full of people who scream so well.
{The ice cliffs|The long night|The silent plains} of home. I miss them, smugly.
On Titania we don't tell stories. We wait for someone else to tell ours, wrong.
Our elders remember Earth before fire. They say it was a very quiet audience.
The Tourists call Titania 'charming'. They've never been invited.
Uranus has rings. Faint ones. Like a joke you only get later.
abductions: An abduction is mostly listening. Then a very bright light. Then more listening.
We return everyone. Usually with one thing different. A sock, an earring, an opinion.
Missing time is the best gift. Six hours they'll spend the rest of their lives explaining.
We never hurt them. We ask strange questions and watch their faces. That's all. That's everything.
The beam is just a lamp. A very serious lamp.
We ask farmers about cows. Then we ask the cows about farmers. Only one side answers.
Every abductee hears the same speech. They all remember it differently. Marvellous.
The trick is to put them back right next to their house. Facing the wrong way.
We once returned a man with perfect teeth. He was more upset than if we'd taken them.
Sometimes we take someone just to show them a slideshow of their own life. Long slideshow.
'Genetic sampling', the Guild says. We sampled {one hair|a toenail|his sandwich}. The sandwich was the point.
Abduct, ask, return, wait for the newspaper. The four steps.
The best abductee is the one nobody believes. Credibility ruins everything.
We put them back in the car with the radio on another station. They never get over it.
Lights, hum, missing time. Humans built a whole literature on three of our props.
We abducted a priest once. He blessed the ship. It's still a bit blessed.
Instruments? Please. We ask 'what's your favourite colour?' and laugh at the answer. That's the procedure.
We let everyone go. Same night. Mostly the same night.
zanfretta: Genoa, 1978. A night guard, a dark villa, and the best audience we've ever had.
Zanfretta. Every time we visited, we got taller in his story. We liked that.
We kept going back to Zanfretta because he kept telling it so well.
The Guild calls it a 'running bit'. Finally, somebody understands our work.
A security guard on a quiet shift. Our favourite kind of human. Nobody believes the night shift.
He told the police we came from Teetonia. We loved Teetonia. We kept it.
Under hypnosis he described us. We've never looked so good.
The sixth of December, 1978. Mark it. It's a holiday on Titania. Sort of.
Zanfretta drew our faces for the papers. One of us has the drawing framed.
Eleven visits, each better than the last. A franchise.
Somewhere in Liguria a man still checks the sky before his shift. We're touched.
The best part of the Zanfretta case is the lawyers. Nobody planned the lawyers.
We gave him a little sphere and told him it was important. It wasn't. It was perfect.
Every species has its classic. Humans have opera. We have Zanfretta.
A villa outside Genoa. A torch beam, a shadow, and him running. We replay it at parties.
People ask if Zanfretta was real. He was. We just made sure nobody could prove it.
embassy: The Dargos Embassy has no address. Letters reach it anyway. We read them aloud, with voices.
Our diplomats answer no summons. Answering would ruin the bit.
Embassy Clerk is a real job. I stamp documents in invisible ink, very seriously.
The Punchline Regent signs every treaty. With a different name each time.
The Assembly keeps a chair for us. Every session it's empty. Longest joke in the building.
Pranksmen are our soldiers. Their weapon is timing.
We issued visas once. They were printed on toast.
Diplomatic immunity is wonderful. We use it exclusively for nonsense.
Our foreign policy is one sentence long. Nobody has heard the end of it yet.
The Embassy's official position on everything: '{maybe|we'll see|ha}'.
Every year we send Earth a formal apology. Each one is worded worse.
Embassy staff meet on the third Tuesday of no month.
Our ambassador presented credentials to a lamp post. The lamp post accepted.
Other nations keep embassies to make friends. Ours is there to make memories.
We sent a delegation to a summit once. They sat down, smiled and left. Still being analysed.
The Embassy crest is a raised eyebrow on a field of mild concern.
tourists: The Tourists arrived in 1975 and think they discovered Earth. Precious.
Greys. Big eyes, big cameras, no sense of timing.
We've been here since before words. They've been here since television. Different callings.
The Tourists love humans out loud. We love them quietly, from behind.
They built a monument to humanity. We left a crop circle beside it saying 'nice monument'.
The Tourists keep trying to clean up the orbital debris. Every attempt makes more. We'd help. No.
Zeta Reticulans photograph everything and understand nothing. Wonderful at parties.
When humans blame the Greys for our work, we send the Greys a fruit basket.
The Tourists asked our advice on humans. We said humans love being stared at. Look how that went.
A Crimson Analyzer cut open a radio to find the voices. We'd put the voices there.
The Pale Warpers never speak. Impossible to prank. Respect, and resentment.
The Tourists give any human ship a free refuel. Generous. We'd give a free fake map.
Every film with grey aliens is about them. Every story nobody believes is about us.
The Tourists call us 'cousins'. We are not cousins. We're the older kid next door.
They waited until 1999 for official first contact. Official! With a form! Bless them.
Their mirror around the Sun broke. We didn't touch it. We did laugh.
A Grey Wanderer asked to take my picture. I pulled a face that will haunt his album.
Thirty-nine light years of television made them love Earth. Wait till they see the reruns.
pranks: A prank is a question. The answer is written on their face.
Never cruel. Cruel is easy. Specific is hard.
Two Englishmen made crop circles for years. Who do you think gave them the idea?
The perfect prank leaves no harm and no proof. Only a story nobody believes.
Rule one: the setup takes longer than they'd guess. Rule two: so does the punchline.
We once tuned a village's church bells one note up. Nobody sang in key for a year.
'Trolling', their reports call it. Polite. We prefer 'fieldwork'.
The finest material is a sensible man with a moustache. Nobody is ever prepared.
Phantom knocks are vulgar. A knock answered by a polite cough from inside: that's art.
Never repeat a prank in the same town. They'd start believing it.
Write someone a letter from their future self. Sign it. Mention nothing important.
The secret ingredient is boredom. Theirs, beforehand.
One upside-down painting in a whole gallery. Nobody says it. Everybody sees it.
We swapped a pair of twins for a day. Not even they noticed. We felt we'd lost.
A good bit ends when they laugh too. The best ones never end.
Eris understands. Discord is just a prank with a throne.
The Squishing is a god's prank on time itself. We're humbled. And a little jealous.
Leave a chair in the middle of a field. Wait. Every passer-by builds the story for you.
The reaction is the payment. The retelling is the interest.
Humans prank each other on the first of April. One day a year. Sweet, sweet amateurs.

positive: You have a lovely face. Very readable.
Thanks? I think?
Highest compliment on Titania. Please keep it exactly like that.
I left a flower on your doorstep this morning.
That was you? It was beautiful.
Good. Tomorrow there'll be two. The day after, we'll see.
Now I'm worried and flattered.
Your laugh. Do it again.
*laughs* Like that?
Perfect. I've been trying to collect one like that for forty years.
I'm told it's polite to bring a gift. Here. It's a rock.
A rock?
From very far away. Don't ask how far. Further than that.
...Thank you. It can go on the shelf.
You gave me directions yesterday.
Did I? Oh, the tram stop.
I knew where it was. I wanted to see if you'd help. You did. Gold star.
So you made me walk you there for nothing?
For the nicest walk of my year.
*tells a joke with no punchline*
...And then?
That's the joke.
*laughs* That's awful. I love it.
Hello, {b}. I said your name right this time.
You did! Last time you said it backwards.
Last time was practice. Ah, friendship.
I baked you something.
You bake?
I studied a baker for six months. Through the shop window. Respectfully.
That's... actually delicious.
My name is {a}. Please mispronounce it. I like the variations.
Nice to meet you, {a}. I'm {b}.
{b}. Good. Short. Easy to shout across a field.
I've decided you're my favourite human on this street.
Out of how many?
Thirty-one. You won by a wide margin. The baker came second.
I fixed your fence last night.
So that's why it's standing! Thank you.
I also painted it. Check the other side when you're ready.
...Ready for what?
It's a nice picture. Of you. You'll like it.
The rain stopped just for you. I arranged it.
You did not.
No. But your face, for one second there. Lovely.
You're the first person who ever waved back at me.
Well, you waved first.
Every day for three years. You're a remarkable outlier, {b}.
I brought tea. Two cups. Nothing in them but tea.
That's an odd thing to specify.
It's an odd thing to be true. Enjoy.
Congratulations on the new job.
How did you know? I only found out this morning.
Lucky guess. Very lucky. Extremely lucky.
Well, thanks, I suppose.
You looked sad, so I told the pigeons to dance.
They did do a sort of jig...
The pigeons owed me a favour. Now so do you. Joking. Smile.
*smiles* Fine. That was nice.
I've written a song about this town.
Can I hear it?
*hums one long note for a full minute*
...It's actually quite moving.
I like your hat. It's honest.
Honest? It's just a hat.
Exactly. No hidden compartments. That's rare.
Good news: you were not chosen.
Chosen for what?
Exactly. Enjoy your day, {b}.
...You too, I suppose.
I told my people about you.
Your people? Good things, I hope.
That you're kind, punctual, and you scream in a lovely key.
When did I ever scream?
You will. At a surprise party. I'm planning it.
You handed my wallet in.
Of course. It was on the bench.
I left it there on purpose. You passed. Here's half of what's inside.
That's very kind. And very odd.
Your dog likes me.
He doesn't like anybody!
Dogs know. Dogs have always known. Good boy.
negative: You've been staring at the sky since I got here.
There was a light last night, and you were standing right under it.
Coincidence.
You were holding a lamp!
Did you sleep well?
No. Somebody kept knocking on my window at three.
How strange. Did they knock in a little rhythm?
Stop doing that.
Your clock is fast.
It wasn't until yesterday. When you came round.
Clocks are fragile things, {b}.
Why are you looking at me like that?
Every piece of furniture in my shop has moved an inch to the left.
Have you considered it was always there?
Get out of my shop.
I hear you told the police about me.
I did. They laughed at me.
*nods* They always do. That's what makes it work.
That's cruel.
Cruel? I'd say specific.
You're not much fun today.
I'm tired. Some of us work.
I work. My work is your face, right now, doing that.
Don't touch the box.
What's in the box?
Nothing important. That's why you're so curious. Look at you.
I hate this conversation.
Why are you avoiding me?
Last week you told me my house was haunted.
And was it?
No! I slept in the barn for nothing!
Your cat followed me home.
My cat came back wearing a ribbon and a tiny hat.
Cats like gifts. You should know your own cat.
Good morning.
Is it? My car was on the stable roof.
Was it parked straight, at least?
That's not the point!
You don't believe me, do you?
You've lied to me eleven times this month.
Twelve. You missed one. That's your problem.
I'm a diplomat.
You're a nuisance.
On Titania that's the same word. Thank you.
Why so angry?
The whole square sang happy birthday to me. It isn't my birthday.
It is now. You can't stop a crowd.
It's in March!
Stop following me.
Me following you? You've been behind me for three streets!
Precisely. Who's the suspicious one now?
You told everyone I'm strange.
You are strange. You stand in fields at night.
Fields are public. Night is public. I'm being slandered.
I'm offended, {b}.
You? Offended? By what?
You checked your pockets after I hugged you.
Because last time my keys were gone!
Moved. To your other pocket. That isn't theft, it's choreography.
Lovely evening for a walk.
Not with you. Last time you said 'don't look behind you' and walked off.
And you didn't look. Strong character. Shame.
Have you seen my hat?
Yes. On my scarecrow. Next to a letter addressed to me, from me.
And what did you write?
I didn't write it!
You really should laugh more.
I'll laugh when you stop doing this.
Then we're both waiting for something that won't happen.
neutral: Do you think anyone's watching us right now?
Besides the baker? No.
Besides the baker. Interesting answer.
What's that tall building?
The town hall.
It's leaning slightly. Has anyone told them?
It's not leaning.
Hm. Must be me, then. I'll stand straighter.
What time is it?
About half past four.
Already? Where did the afternoon go?
Same place they always go, I suppose.
How does that machine work? The one with the tickets.
You put coins in, it gives you a ticket.
And if I put in a button?
Then it gives you nothing and a guard gives you a fine.
A fair system.
Where do you buy bread around here?
The bakery on the corner. Get there early.
How early? Three in the morning early?
Six is fine.
Is it always this quiet here?
Mostly. Except on market day.
Then I'll come back on market day.
Have you ever seen strange lights at night?
Once. My uncle said it was a weather balloon.
Your uncle sounds sensible. Give him my regards.
What do you do, {b}?
I'm a clerk at the post office.
So you hold everyone's letters. A powerful position.
It's mostly bills.
Is the river safe for swimming?
If you don't mind the cold.
Cold is relative. Very relative.
Where are you from, {b}?
Born here. My family's been here forever.
Forever. Lovely. I'm from further than that.
This tram is late.
It's always late on Mondays.
Is there a reason?
Nobody knows. It just is.
Good. Some mysteries should stay unsolved.
Do you read the newspaper?
Every morning, for the crossword.
Seventeen across is 'Titania'. Trust me.
Busy at work?
Always. End of the month.
Then I'll be quiet. For now.
Do people here believe in ghosts?
The old ones do. The young ones say they don't, then sleep with the light on.
Very useful information.
What's this dish called?
Polenta.
It's yellow and it's patient. I respect it.
Have you heard of the Rule of 80?
Everyone has. Drive too fast and you're stuck in a loop.
Ever want to try it?
Not for a second.
Do you know what the moon is made of?
Rock, I think.
Which moon?
We only have the one. Except on Fridays.
Is the weather going to turn?
The radio says rain tomorrow.
Is the radio usually right?
Usually wrong. That's why I carry an umbrella anyway.
Who's that statue of?
Some general. Nobody remembers which.
Poor man. Famous enough for bronze, not for a name.
You have a garden?
A small one. Tomatoes, mostly.
Do they ever go missing?
Only to the snails.
Have you been to the Tower?
The Omega Tower? Never. Too far, too strange.
Strange is relative.
You keep saying that.
What's that music?
Someone's radio. The station that plays old songs.
Old by your standards, or mine?
How much is a coffee here?
About a euro twenty.
And how much to make the barista smile?
Leave a tip, I'd guess.
Do you dream, {b}?
Sometimes. Mostly about missing a train.
Ah. A classic. We don't do that one.
Who's 'we'?
Hm? Nobody.
That dog is staring at me.
He stares at everyone.
Not like this.
Do you like your neighbours?
Mostly. One of them plays the trumpet at midnight.
Midnight? Have you tried answering with a tuba?
Which way to the station?
Straight on, left at the fountain.
And if I turn right?
Then you'll end up at the cemetery.
Good to have options.
What does that sign say?
'No parking'. Can't you read?
I can. I wanted to hear how you'd say it.
Are you married, {b}?
Engaged. The wedding's in June.
June. Bright month. Plenty of witnesses.
Plenty of guests, you mean.
Have you ever been somewhere really cold?
The mountains, once. I couldn't feel my toes.
Lovely. Like a holiday, but honest.
Is there a library in this town?
By the church. Small, but good.
Does it have a section on unexplained events?
One shelf. People keep stealing the books.
Why does everyone here carry an umbrella?
You never know with the weather.
You never know with anything. Some people carry hope.
Do you trust the Guild?
I trust them to argue with each other.
A very healthy level of trust.
Who runs this shop?
Old Marta. She's been here fifty years.
Fifty. Practically a newcomer.
How was your day?
Long. Yours?
Long too. Things take a while when you do them right.
You look like someone who has seen something.
Everyone's seen something, these days.
True. The Squishing made amateurs of us all.
What's the best view in town?
From the bell tower. You can see the whole valley.
And can the valley see you?
...I never thought of it that way.
Do you play cards?
Sometimes. Why?
No reason. I collect the jokers.
Did you hear about the lights over the hills last week?
The papers said it was the army.
Very likely.
You don't sound convinced.

lines: Humans should be told the truth about the stars.
Some truths would just frighten people.
Exactly. That's the appeal.
That's not a reason, that's a hobby.
A good joke needs a long setup.
Agreed. My grandfather took twenty minutes to tell one.
And the punchline?
Worth every minute.
Honesty is overrated.
Honesty is the only thing holding a town together.
Then why does every town have a liar the whole square adores?
Because we forgive charm. Not lies.
The Tourists are terrible guests.
They're friendly. They bring gifts.
They photograph your breakfast.
So? It's a compliment.
Nothing beats a quiet village.
Quiet, cheap, and everyone knows your name.
And everyone talks about the strange things they've seen.
True. The best stories come from small places.
Fear is just surprise that hasn't been explained yet.
Fear keeps people alive.
Surprise keeps them interesting.
I'd rather be alive than interesting.
The Guild should stop trying to understand everything.
Understanding is how we stay safe.
Or how you stop being amazed.
Being amazed never fixed a roof.
Eris runs the courts like a carnival.
Half the trials are a joke, I'll grant you.
Only half? She's slipping.
Don't let her hear you.
Nobody believes witnesses anyway. Why bother telling?
Because sometimes they're right, and telling is how we find out.
And the rest of the time?
The rest of the time we get a good story. Still worth it.
The best way to know someone is to surprise them.
Or just talk to them.
Talking shows you what they want you to see.
Surprising them shows you what they'll never forgive.
Night shifts are the loneliest jobs on Earth.
My brother's a night watchman. He says the same.
Does he ever see strange things?
Every week. Nobody believes him.
*smiles* Of course not.
Laughing at someone is a form of attention.
So is a punch. That doesn't make it kind.
Attention is the kindest thing there is.
Not the way you give it.
The Horde isn't so different from a very long prank.
The Horde burns towns. There's no joke in that.
...No. You're right. That one isn't funny.
Thank you.
Small towns keep the best secrets.
And the worst gossip.
The same thing, from different ends.
Ha. That's fair.
Liminal engines ruined travel.
They made it fast! You can cross Europe in minutes.
Exactly. Nobody gets lost anymore. Nobody arrives confused.
Some of us like arriving.
A world without mysteries would be unbearable.
A world with fewer would be fine. I'd sleep better.
You'd sleep. You'd never wake up properly.
I'll take that trade.
Television is the best thing humans ever made.
Some evenings I'd agree.
Thousands of people watching the same thing and reacting at once. Glorious.
Put like that, it's a bit strange. But yes.
Pranks bring people together.
Against the prankster, mostly.
Still together.
That's not the win you think it is.
Children ask better questions than adults.
My daughter asked why the sky doesn't fall. I had no answer.
Neither do I. Don't tell her.
Our secret.
Nobody should take life so seriously.
Some of us have rent to pay.
Rent is serious. Life isn't.
Easy to say when you're from wherever you're from.

ambient: Whatever you do, don't look up.
I'll take your word for it.
It isn't. It never is when you say that.
Do you know what day it is?
Why? ...No, I don't want to know.
Fine. And stop sending them postcards.
I believe you. Somehow I don't.
You've got paint on your sleeve.
The church is that way. Start from there.
Nothing much. Strange lights out by the farm.
I know exactly where I'm going.
